clusters.intent: Design real-time 3D scenes through rendering stages, shader and lighting choices, collision abstractions, camera behavior, and distance-based detail budgets.
clusters.rationale: The two engine-neutral reviews cover the same 3D scene, rendering, collision, camera, lighting, and LOD mechanism; one canonical member and one variant preserve the evidence without duplicate ownership.

clusters.intent: Adapt game controls, rendering, lifecycle, thermal degradation, and release planning to constrained touch devices and mobile distribution boundaries.
clusters.rationale: Touch interaction, pause and lifecycle handling, thermal degradation, device performance, and store readiness form one mobile specialization with explicit shipping authority boundaries.

clusters.intent: Design immersive interaction around comfort, stable frame timing, scale and depth cues, locomotion, and controller or hand-tracking affordances.
clusters.rationale: The review binds player comfort, movement choice, spatial perception, tracked input, and frame-time consistency into a distinct immersive-experience acceptance surface.

clusters.intent: Structure engine-neutral 2D scenes with atlases, tile layers, simplified collision, genre movement, camera response, and deterministic teardown of embedded guests.
clusters.rationale: Both reviews describe the same 2D runtime responsibilities and cleanup boundaries with complementary wording, so they form one canonical mechanism and one variant.

clusters.intent: Turn a game concept into a testable player loop, compact design brief, progression model, pacing hypothesis, and evidence-led playtest balancing cycle.
clusters.rationale: The two reviews share the same core-loop, mechanics, progression, motivation, pacing, and playtest feedback contract and should not become parallel direction skills.

clusters.intent: Apply version-matched Godot project, scene, signal, GDScript, optimization, and reference-lookup practices.
clusters.rationale: The useful architecture patterns are coupled to one engine version, language, documentation surface, and dependency environment, so they remain a specialist adapter rather than portable Arcadia behavior.

clusters.intent: Select a browser rendering stack and coordinate progressive assets, visibility lifecycle, audio activation, offline packaging, hybrid interfaces, and teardown.
clusters.rationale: The reviewed mechanism is coherent but spans changing browser APIs, framework guests, offline packaging, audio policies, and deployment choices that require a separate current web-runtime contract.
